study: D1: calibrated leading-order scaling, not a fluid simulation

reference.h_interpretation: inverse-law limit h -> 0+, not an admissible theorem instance
reference.calibration_status: illustrative SI reference pair; profile and viscosity compatibility not established
reference.gradient_interpretation: L_grad = beta*r_c is an assumed screening proxy, not evaluated from the velocity field

sensitivity.necessary_h_ceiling_source: Lemma 4.8 p.35: h < exp(-T_d), T_d = exp(M_d)+10 > 10; hence h < exp(-10). This is only a necessary ceiling, not an admissible chosen h.
sensitivity.h_interpretation: exponent-only sweep; no claim that any finite chosen h satisfies the full proof hierarchy
sensitivity.normalization_interpretation: alternative effective r0; exactly degenerate with reference-radius uncertainty, not an independent error bar

screening.notes: Mach and Kn markers are screening conventions. Liquid spacing multiples are geometric markers, not a validated continuum threshold. Liquid relaxation data and actual strain are not evaluated.

constants.edition: CODATA 2022; c, N_A and k_B are exact SI constants; a0 rounded from CODATA

air.locator: Equation (11) and Table 3, printed p. 35 / PDF p. 5
air.notes: Dry-air reference. Mean free path uses the NIST paper's convention. Density and sound speed are ideal-gas estimates using rounded R and gamma assumptions, not additional measured NIST values. Properties are frozen for screening, not evolved along collapse.

water.notes: Liquid-water reference at 25 C and 0.1 MPa. n^(-1/3) is a mean-spacing estimate. Viscosity and sound speed are frozen reference values, not a high-speed equation of state.
